name: Acourtia

shared_genus_characters.look_here_first: First decide whether leaves form a deeply lobed basal rosette or grow along branched leafy stems. Confirm with head arrangement, disk floret count and phyllary tips.
shared_genus_characters.shared: Perennial Asteraceae with rayless pink/lavender heads and pappus-bearing cypselae. Color is not a reliable separator.

local_lookalike_cautions: A. microcephala has spinulose leaf teeth and pointed/mucronate phyllaries; count overlap makes phyllaries essential.
A. nana has small rounded hollylike leaves.
look_here_first: Find the BASE of the plant and follow its leaves upward. A deeply pinnately lobed basal rosette with mostly leafless flowering scapes points to A. runcinata; unlobed toothed leaves along taller branched stems point to A. wrightii. Then check head floret counts and phyllary tips on a mature head; flower color is shared.

shared_traits: Perennial members of Asteraceae: each apparent flower head is a capitulum made of multiple disk florets, without ray florets in the two installed species.
Heads are subtended by overlapping involucral bracts (phyllaries); their tip shapes provide supporting species-level characters.
Leaves are toothed to divided, but where the leaves are carried (basal rosette versus leafy stem) is more informative than the color of the heads.
Fruits are cypselae with a pappus; photograph mature fruits when available rather than relying on petal color.
priority: 1 · Photograph the plant BASE and the first 20–30 cm of stem: basal rosette and mostly leafless scapes versus tall branched leafy stems.
2 · Photograph an intact mid-stem leaf with its attachment: deeply pinnately lobed basal leaves versus unlobed dentate alternate cauline leaves.
3 · Photograph multiple mature heads: 1–3 relatively large heads versus clusters of smaller heads.
4 · On a head face count disk florets: canonical accounts give 25–53 for A. runcinata and 8–12 for A. wrightii; use intact mature heads.
5 · Turn the head sideways and magnify phyllary tips: long-tapering acuminate versus blunt to shortly acute.
study_strategy.warning: Both are rayless, pink/lavender-headed composites. A close-up of the colored head alone cannot show basal-versus-cauline foliage. Species counts and phyllary tips follow the settled canonical cards; do not extrapolate to unreviewed Acourtia taxa.

quick_key.if: Deeply pinnately lobed leaves concentrated in a basal rosette; mostly leafless scapes; usually 1–3 heads with 25–53 disk florets and acuminate phyllaries
Alternate, unlobed but dentate leaves distributed along taller branched stems; clustered heads with about 8–12 disk florets and blunt to shortly acute phyllaries
Only a flower-head close-up, incomplete leaf base, or immature heads are visible
quick_key.then: Leave as Acourtia sp. until leaf architecture and mature head details are available

comparison_cards.title: Featherleaf desertpeony vs brownfoot
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Photograph the entire plant from ground level before zooming into the flower heads: where are the leaves, and are the flowering stalks leafy?

field_matrix.runcinata: Basal rosette; deeply pinnately lobed leaves
field_matrix.wrightii: Alternate cauline leaves on branched stems; blades unlobed but dentate
Taller branched, leafy flowering stems (canonical habit 30–150 cm)
Heads grouped in clusters on branched stems

field_matrix.strength: high supporting count; use mature, intact heads

field_matrix.wrightii: Obtuse to shortly acute, blunt to short-pointed

field_matrix.runcinata: Ray florets absent; pink/lavender disk heads
field_matrix.wrightii: Ray florets absent; pink/lavender disk heads

comparison_cards.caution: Color and raylessness are shared. Detached heads can conceal the strongest distinction: leaf distribution. A. microcephala can resemble brownfoot and may overlap in head counts; verify its sharper leaf teeth and pointed/mucronate phyllaries in an authoritative key before species assignment.

overlap_cautions: Both canonical species lack ray florets and may have pink/lavender heads; color is not a species-level decision.
Do not use a detached head to infer whether foliage is basal or cauline. Capture the whole plant and the stem base.
Counts of disk florets require mature intact heads and correct counting of individual florets, not petals or phyllaries.
Phyllary tip shape is best viewed from the side; damage or immature tips can imitate a shorter point.
Acourtia microcephala and A. nana are comparison-only names in this lesson, not newly admitted or confirmed local species.
Both installed species retain UNRESOLVED target-zone native-range status; no range or taxonomy decisions are changed.

local_lookalikes.separate_by: Compare leaf-margin spinulose teeth and pointed or mucronate phyllaries; do not rely on head-floret counts alone.

local_lookalikes.separate_by: Look for small rounded, hollylike leaves rather than the deeply lobed basal rosette or taller leafy stems.
Confirm capitulum and phyllary architecture; then use Acourtia leaf placement, mature heads and cypselae rather than color.
